name: All Fives (Dominoes)
description: All Fives is the quintessential American domino game. Played with a double-six set, it challenges players to create 'scoring ends' that sum to a multiple of five. It is a game of rapid math, blocking, and tactical placement.

overview.description: All Fives is the quintessential American domino game. Played with a double-six set, it challenges players to create 'scoring ends' that sum to a multiple of five. It is a game of rapid math, blocking, and tactical placement.

history.origins: Derived from traditional European tile games, All Fives gained immense popularity in North America in the late 19th century. It is often referred to as 'Muggins' when played without the rule to call out scores.
timeline: 1880s: Muggins rules first standardized in American game manuals.
1920s: The 'Five Up' variant (using all doubles as spinners) becomes popular in the West Coast USA.
Modern: Standard game for professional domino tournaments in the US.
history.cultural: Used as a competitive social game in clubs and barbershops across the US. A specialized 'domino cribbage' board is often used for scoring.
history.evolution: Shifted from a simple 'blocking' game to a point-rich strategic game where players calculate 2-3 moves ahead to maximize 'multiple of 5' scoring.

setup.players: 2 players (7 tiles each) or 4 players in partnerships (5 tiles each).
setup.dealing: Tiles are 'washed' (shuffled) face down. Players draw their hand; remaining tiles are the 'Boneyard'.
setup.equipment: Domino set, score sheet or scoreboard.

rules.objective: Be the first to reach the target score (usually 100, 200, or 250) by creating end-totals that are multiples of five.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Leading**: Any tile can be led. 2. **Matching**: Subsequent tiles must match the pips of an open end. 3. **Doubles**: Placed crosswise. They count as the sum of their pips until matched on both sides. 4. **The Spinner**: The first double played is the 'Spinner'. Once matched on its sides, tiles can be played off its ends, creating 4 open ends. 5. **Scoring**: After playing a tile, sum all open ends. If the total is a multiple of 5 (5, 10, 15, 20, etc.), the player immediately scores that many points. 6. **Boneyard**: If you cannot play, you must draw from the boneyard until you can. 7. **Dominoing**: The hand ends when a player uses their last tile. They score the remaining pips in their opponents' hands (rounded to the nearest 5).
keyRules: Must play if able. You cannot draw from the boneyard if you have a legal play.
Only the first double is a spinner. All other doubles are 'dead' once matched.
Muggins: If a player fails to claim a scoring total, an opponent may shout 'Muggins!' and take the points for themselves.
If the game is blocked (no one can play), the player with the lowest pip total wins the hand bonus.

strategy.basic: Always look for plays that sum to 10 or 15. The 5-5 (double-five) tile is the strongest opener as it scores 10 points immediately.
strategy.intermediate: Blocking: If you have many 4s but your opponent is low, try to keep an open 4 on the board while matching other ends to suits you control.
strategy.advanced: The 'End Control': If three ends are 6, 4, and 5 (Total 15), look for a play that changes the 6/4 to something that keeps the total as a multiple of 5 (e.g., matching the 6 with a 6-1 to make the ends 1, 4, 5 = 10).
tips: Keep track of the 0-0 (double-blank) tile. It is a powerful reset for end totals.
If playing partnerships, try to leave ends that your partner has expressed interest in by their previous draws.

variations.name: Five Up
variations.description: West Coast variant where every double is a spinner, potentially creating a many-armed layout.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Five Up changes which doubles act as spinners; base scoring and flow stay the same.

variations.name: Sniff
variations.description: A variant where the first double *can* be used as a spinner, but only after it has been played off of.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Sniff adjusts spinner usage and timing but keeps the same deck, players, and scoring structure.

scoring.description: Points are scored both during play and at the end of the hand.
scoring.winCondition: First player/team to reach 250 points (standard) Wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Tackle the most popular domino game in the world. Calculate your ends, play your doubles, and race to 250 points in this deep, tactical battle of tiles.
